text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 25 in history.
1154 - King Stephen of England died and was succeeded by Henry II, thus establishing the house of Plantagenet.
1400 - Geoffrey Chaucer, English poet best known for his unfinished "Canterbury Tales", died.
1415 - Henry V of England defeated the French at the Battle of Agincourt in northern France.
1825 - Johann Strauss (the Younger) born. Austrian composer known as the "Waltz King," famous for his Viennese waltzes, notably "The Blue Danube".

1854 - In the Crimean War at the battle of Balaclava, Lord Cardigan led the cavalry charge of the Light Brigade against the Russians, one of the most heroic episodes in British military history. 272 out of 673 were killed in the charge.
1838 - Georges Bizet born. French composer famous for his opera "Carmen" whose bad reception hastened his death in 1875.
1881 - Pablo Picasso born. Spanish artist and sculptor. One of the most influential, controversial and pioneering artists of the 20th century.
1955 - By this day all Allied occupation forces had left Austria and it resumed sovereignty for the first time since the German occupation of 1938.
1971 - General Assembly of the United Nations voted to admit China to the U.N. and to expel Taiwan.
1983 - An assault force led by U.S. marines, backed by token contingents from seven English-speaking Caribbean countries, invaded Grenada.
1995 - Israel furthered a peace deal with the PLO by beginning the redeployment of its West Bank troops.
